id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-9" value="stripe" style="shape=module;align=left;spacingLeft=20;align=center;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="380" y="480" width="100" height="50" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-11" value="abstratium<div>abstraccount</div>" style="shape=module;align=left;spacingLeft=20;align=center;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="470" y="660" width="100" height="50" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-12" value="" style="shape=cylinder3;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;boundedLbl=1;backgroundOutline=1;size=15;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="590" y="670" width="60" height="80" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-18" value="<div>Even though JWT says user is in Org B, the o<span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">ffer goes into org A because it is for product P in org A.</span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">abstrapact can do the lookup of the orgId out of the product, so has not trust issues. Any product that can be sold publicly can be given as input, but that is not a worry because a threat actor could also just create an offer using the b2c client.</span></div>" style="shape=note2;boundedLbl=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;size=9;verticalAlign=top;align=center;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="793" y="267.5" width="190" height="185" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-20" style="rounded=0;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;dashed=1;endArrow=none;startFill=0;" edge="1" parent="1" source="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-18" target="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-2"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="653" y="366" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="603" y="362" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-21" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=0;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;entryX=0.5;entryY=0;entryDx=0;entryDy=0;entryPerimeter=0;" edge="1" parent="1" source="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-4" target="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-5"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-25" style="rounded=0;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;dashed=1;endArrow=none;startFill=0;" edge="1" parent="1" source="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-26" target="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-12"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="670" y="716" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-26" value="- payment in Org A" style="shape=note2;boundedLbl=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;size=9;verticalAlign=top;align=center;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="693" y="690" width="120" height="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-27" value="<div>We need to be able to ensure that no Threat Actor can create false accounting records.<br>abstraccount needs Org A in the call (since the accounting record needs to be for the Org that owns the product) and it has to be able to trust that it is allowed to write in that Org.</div><div><br></div>Call 70 should not be done in the context of the user in Org B using a token exchange, because it requires all users to be given a role which is public, meaning that anyone in the world could call abstraccount to create a payment record in any Org they choose.<div><br><div>So call 70 should be done using a client-credentials token (which will contain Org C, because Org C created the client). The role in abstraccount shouldn't be publicly available in abstrauth and only assigned to the abstrapact client.<br></div></div>" style="shape=note2;boundedLbl=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;size=9;verticalAlign=top;align=center;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="603" y="475" width="547" height="185" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-28" value="Applications are hosted by a user in Org C, meaning that the client ID of each application are in Org C and any client_credentials sign-in will lead to a JWT containing Org C" style="shape=note2;boundedLbl=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;size=9;verticalAlign=top;align=center;fillColor=#fad7ac;strokeColor=#b46504;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="540" y="100" width="230" height="100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-29" value="Call 50 should be given a UUID that is unknown outside of abstrapact and abstrapact should assert during call 60 that it can find the contract using that ID. That way it is impossible for a threat actor to make call 60 and hit existing data. It will be impossible anyway as they won't have the key that Stripe uses to sign the payload. But an additional layer of security can't hurt." style="shape=note2;boundedLbl=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;size=9;verticalAlign=top;align=center;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="80" y="360" width="250" height="160" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-30" value="" style="endArrow=none;dashed=1;html=1;rounded=0;" edge="1" parent="1" source="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-29"> <mxGeometry width="50" height="50" relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="270" y="680" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="390" y="400" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-31" value="" style="endArrow=none;dashed=1;html=1;rounded=0;" edge="1" parent="1" target="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-27"> <mxGeometry width="50" height="50" relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="560" y="460" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="400" y="410" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-32" value="" style="endArrow=none;dashed=1;html=1;rounded=0;" edge="1" parent="1" source="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-29"> <mxGeometry width="50" height="50" relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="340" y="433" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="440" y="420" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-33" value="How can a threat actor insert false accounting records?<div><br></div><div>i) call abstraccount directly. Mitigated by the interface being protected by a role that is not publicly available and only given to machine accounts. A Threat Actor in Org D cannot create a client-to-client role, since they have no access to Clients in Org C like abstraccount. So we can guarantee that only abstrapact can call abstraccount! abstraccount can fully trust call 70 because it knows that the operators wouldn't give any user or machine outside of its Org C, the role that is necessary to make call 70. The role MUST not be a publicly available role, otherwise users in other Orgs could assign it to themselves!</div><div><br></div><div>ii) Threat actors could call abstrapact and simulate what the b2c client would do. Mitigated in that abstrapact will always take the orgId of the org that created the product, and pass that to abstraccount as the orgId in which to write the accounting records.</div><div><br></div><div>iii) Threat actors could attack the b2c client but again, whatever product they choose, its orgId is what abstrapact will send to abstraccount. So mitigated as in point ii).</div>" style="shape=note2;boundedLbl=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;size=9;verticalAlign=top;align=center;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="30" y="610" width="390" height="310" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-34" value="Threat Actor<div>Org D</div>" style="shape=umlActor;verticalLabelPosition=bottom;verticalAlign=top;html=1;outlineConnect=0;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="10" y="410" width="30" height="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-47" value="Calls 60 &amp; 70 must be idempotent and not create duplicate data." style="shape=note2;boundedLbl=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;size=9;verticalAlign=top;align=center;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="80" y="537.5" width="250" height="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-48" value="Call 70 needs to hit an endpoint in abstraccount which can write to any given orgId. This requires using non-multitenant code and entities without hibernates @TenantId annotation. The orgId of the accounting record (a "transaction" in abstraccount parlance) must be set using the value in the payload.<br><br>The description of the "transaction" should contain the references like contract ID so that it can be reconciled." style="shape=note2;boundedLbl=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;size=9;verticalAlign=top;align=center;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="440" y="820" width="390" height="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-49" style="rounded=0;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;dashed=1;endArrow=none;startFill=0;" edge="1" parent="1" source="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-48" target="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-11"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="660" y="722" as="targetPoint" /> <mxPoint x="703" y="725" as="sourcePoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-50" value="" style="endArrow=none;html=1;rounded=0;strokeWidth=12;fillColor=#fad7ac;strokeColor=#b46504;" edge="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry width="50" height="50" relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="470" y="750" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="550" y="310" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-51" value="Call 70 will NOT be implemented, but is a manual step done periodically by users, e.g. when they take payments out of Stripe. They can create a single bulk-transaction in abstraccount to cover all of their sales in the period." style="shape=note2;boundedLbl=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;size=9;verticalAlign=top;align=center;fillColor=#fad7ac;strokeColor=#b46504;" vertex="1" parent="1"> <mxGeometry x="950" y="810" width="203" height="150" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-52" style="rounded=0;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;dashed=1;endArrow=none;startFill=0;" edge="1" parent="1" source="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-51" target="m4PDLlS1XSzxBt23xrV5-11"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="544" y="720" as="targetPoint" /> <mxPoint x="606" y="830" as="sourcePoint" /> <Array as="points"> <mxPoint x="860" y="780" /> <mxPoint x="610" y="780" /> </Array> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
We need to be able to ensure that no Threat Actor can create false accounting records.
abstraccount needs Org A in the call (since the accounting record needs to be for the Org that owns the product) and it has to be able to trust that it is allowed to write in that Org.
Call 70 should not be done in the context of the user in Org B using a token exchange, because it requires all users to be given a role which is public, meaning that anyone in the world could call abstraccount to create a payment record in any Org they choose.
So call 70 should be done using a client-credentials token (which will contain Org C, because Org C created the client). The role in abstraccount shouldn't be publicly available in abstrauth and only assigned to the abstrapact client.

div.div: Call 50 should be given a UUID that is unknown outside of abstrapact and abstrapact should assert during call 60 that it can find the contract using that ID. That way it is impossible for a threat actor to make call 60 and hit existing data. It will be impossible anyway as they won't have the key that Stripe uses to sign the payload. But an additional layer of security can't hurt.

div.div:
How can a threat actor insert false accounting records?
i) call abstraccount directly. Mitigated by the interface being protected by a role that is not publicly available and only given to machine accounts. A Threat Actor in Org D cannot create a client-to-client role, since they have no access to Clients in Org C like abstraccount. So we can guarantee that only abstrapact can call abstraccount! abstraccount can fully trust call 70 because it knows that the operators wouldn't give any user or machine outside of its Org C, the role that is necessary to make call 70. The role MUST not be a publicly available role, otherwise users in other Orgs could assign it to themselves!
ii) Threat actors could call abstrapact and simulate what the b2c client would do. Mitigated in that abstrapact will always take the orgId of the org that created the product, and pass that to abstraccount as the orgId in which to write the accounting records.
iii) Threat actors could attack the b2c client but again, whatever product they choose, its orgId is what abstrapact will send to abstraccount. So mitigated as in point ii).

div.div:
Call 70 needs to hit an endpoint in abstraccount which can write to any given orgId. This requires using non-multitenant code and entities without hibernates @TenantId annotation. The orgId of the accounting record (a "transaction" in abstraccount parlance) must be set using the value in the payload.
The description of the "transaction" should contain the references like contract ID so that it can be reconciled.
